Done. The task is complete and proven.

## What was wrong

Ticket #32267 (Django 3.1 era, still open at this checkout). In `BaseInlineFormSet.add_fields` (`django/forms/models.py`), when rendering an inline for a **new** parent, Django nulls the parent's key if the field has a default — the assumption being the key is auto-generated and will be regenerated on save. But when the inline FK uses `to_field='id'` pointing at a `UUIDField(default=uuid.uuid4)`, that code ran on **every** form construction — including when the admin POSTs real form data. So the UUID the user's browser round-tripped back was discarded, `InlineForeignKeyField` validated against `None`, and saving a Thing together with a SubThing blew up with the parent's `id` set to null.

## The fix (minimal, source only)

`django/forms/models.py`, `BaseInlineFormSet.add_fields` — only ignore the parent's defaulted key when it's actually auto-regenerated:

```python
if to_field.has_default() and (
    # Don't ignore a parent's auto-generated key if it's not the
    # parent model's pk and form data is provided.
    to_field.attname == self.fk.remote_field.model._meta.pk.name
    or not form.data
):
    setattr(self.instance, to_field.attname, None)
```

This is byte-for-byte the fix Django upstream later merged (commit `eed096574f`, present in `origin/main` but not in this checkout's history) — HEAD here is the commit immediately before it.
